newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cintra operating results improve.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cintra operating results improve.

text.p: Cintra SA, the holding company for Mexico's two biggest airlines, on Thursday said its first-quarter net income almost halved under Mexican accounting rules but its operating income rose by more than 15 percent.

In addition, the company said its Aeromexico and Mexicana de Aviacion airlines showed improvement in terms of key operating measures, such as passenger load factors operating income and costs per available seat kilometer.

Cintra said in a statement its net profit declined mostly because of a sharp reduction in the gains from monetary position -- a Mexican accounting line that reflects the erosion of the purchasing power of the peso.

"Integral cost of financing provided income of 157 million pesos for the 1997 first quarter, compared with 626 million for the same 1996 period," the company said. "This effect was caused by the gain in monetary position...that benefits highly-leveraged companies in inflationary environments.
"The 1996 results were benefited by gains from monetary position in Mexicana, which was highly leveraged during most of the first quarter 1996," it said.
Operating income, which does not include the integral cost of financing, rose 15.7 percent to 401 million pesos from 347 million, the company said.
Cintra cautioned that it integrated the two airlines on June 28, 1996, so the first-quarter comparisons were against combined consolidated 1996 results for Aeromexico and Mexicana.
Aeromexico's passenger load factor improved to 60.89 percent from 57.58 percent a year earlier. Mexicana's load factor rose to 66.58 percent against 62.32 percent.

Available seat kilometers increased for both airlines because of aircraft added to their fleets. Costs per available seat kilometer fell at Mexicana to 0.358 of a peso from 0.385, and dropped marginally to 0.367 at Aeromexico against 0.368.
Aeromexico now flies 54 aircraft, up from 51 a year ago, and Mexicana 47 -- one in major overhaul -- against 44. The group now serves more than 90 cities in the Americas and Europe.
Total staff numbers dipped to 11,479 employees in the first quarter from 11,605 a year earlier.
